newsitem.title: USA: Advanced Micro reports second quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Advanced Micro reports second quarter profit.

text.p: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. Tuesday reported weaker-than-expected second quarter profits, reflecting the rapid shift toward newer generation semiconductors and pricing pressure on older models.

For the three months ended June 29, Advanced Micro earned $9.97 million or 7 cents per fully diluted share on sales of $594.56 million compared with a loss of $34.67 million or 26 cents a share on sales of $455.08 milion a year ago.
The second quarter profit compares with the First Call consensus estimate of 22 cents a share.

A spokesman for the chipmaker attributed the shortfall to the rapid shift toward AMD's newer chip, the K6, pricing pressure in the flash memory business and a disappointing quarter from its programmable logic business unti Vantis.

He said the shift toward chips with so-called MMX technology, which improves the video and graphics on computers, was expected as computer makers phase out older models. The company said it is quickly converting production to the K6 chip.

"We are executing well on our production ramp toward our goal of shipping millions of units in the second half of 1997," the company said. "Our overall book-to-bill ratio was greater than parity, resulting from strong bookings for the AMD-K6 MMX enhanced processor."
